If Antarctica melted completely, the sea would rise about fifty eight metres.
Antarctica holds around ninety percent of the ice on Earth. Nowhere else is close.
Fifty eight metres is not a flood. It is a new map.
But fifty eight is not the number that matters.
About one in ten people alive live less than ten metres above the sea.
So the damage is not waiting at the end. Most of it lands in the first few metres.
The full melt takes thousands of years. The first metre does not.
Nobody is planning for fifty eight. They are watching the first one.
Which is a long way of saying the boring hill behind your town is about to get expensive.
